note: Setup rating overrides, read by prefill/assemble.mjs. By default a project is 'Easy setup' when it is an app (install like a normal app or open in a browser) and 'Advanced setup' when it is server software, a developer tool or a code library. The rating is about the software itself, never about someone else's hosted copy (Destin, Oct 27: a free hosted version doesn't make the software easy to set up). 'easy' lists projects whose default kind hides a normal installable app, or that are themselves a public website; 'advanced' lists apps that still take real effort to set up. One reason each; reasons are shown on the project page.

easy.stirling-pdf: It has desktop installers for Windows, Mac and Linux that you install like any other program.
easy.openstreetmap: It is a website: you use it at openstreetmap.org in a browser.
easy.open-library: It is a website: you use it at openlibrary.org in a browser.
easy.onlyoffice-docs: ONLYOFFICE makes a free desktop app (ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors) for Windows, Mac and Linux that you install like any other program; only the shared online editor needs a server.
easy.glazewm: It has an installer for Windows that you run like any other program.
easy.godot: It is a desktop program you download and open; no server or command line needed.
easy.ghidra: It is a desktop program you download and open, though it is aimed at specialists.
easy.crystal: It is a desktop app you install like any other program.
easy.headlamp: It has a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux.
easy.cyberchef: It is a website: you use it in a browser with nothing to install.
easy.jamovi: It has desktop installers for Windows, Mac and Linux.
easy.lighthouse: It is built into Chrome: open the browser's developer tools and choose Lighthouse to get a report.
